name: Oven: Roasting, Baking & Broiling
summary: Roasting vs. baking vs. broiling, convection, rack positions and the reverse sear.

rows: Vegetables, chicken pieces and whole chickens, small roasts: browns the outside well.
Big roasts and turkeys, which need time for heat to reach the middle without the outside overcooking.
Cakes, cookies, breads, casseroles. The temperature matters more here; follow the recipe.
Melting cheese, browning tops, thin fish and steaks. Fast: watch it the whole time.

sections.heading: Oven basics

items: **Preheat fully.** Most ovens take 10–15 minutes; many beep before the walls are really hot.
**Middle rack** unless the recipe says otherwise. Lower racks brown bottoms (pizza, crisp vegetables); upper racks brown tops.
**Give food space.** Vegetables in one layer with room between pieces roast; piled up, they steam. Use two pans rather than one crowded one.
**Rimmed sheet pans** for roasting, so juices don't drip onto the oven floor.
**Ovens run hot or cold.** An inexpensive oven thermometer tells you how far off yours is.

blocks: Baking? [Oven and Pans](guide:oven-and-pans) covers pan materials and sizes, and rack positions for cakes and cookies.

sections.heading: Convection
blocks: A convection (fan) setting blows hot air around, so food cooks and browns faster and more evenly. For a recipe written for a regular oven, lower the temperature by about 25°F (15°C), or keep it and start checking about a quarter of the way early.
It's great for roasting and anything you want crisp. For delicate bakes (custards, soufflés, some cakes) the moving air can dry or tilt them; use the regular setting unless the recipe says otherwise.
Cooking at a different temperature than the recipe says, because something else is in the oven? The [Oven Time Converter](tool:/utils/oven-time) estimates the new time.

sections.heading: Broiling
blocks: The broiler is an upside-down grill. Put the rack so the food's top sits about 3–4 inches (8–10 cm) below the element, preheat it for 5 minutes, and keep the door where your recipe or manual says (some ovens broil with the door cracked).

blocks.text: Stay at the oven while broiling: food goes from browned to burnt in under a minute. Don't broil in glass baking dishes, which can shatter under direct heat.

sections.heading: The reverse sear
blocks: For thick steaks (1 ½ inches (4 cm) or more) and small roasts, cook low first, then sear: you get even doneness from edge to center and a crisp crust.

items: Season the meat and put it on a rack over a sheet pan in a 250°F (120°C) oven.
Roast until it's about 10–15°F (5–8°C) below your target on the [doneness chart](guide:doneness-and-food-safety#doneness-chart), usually 30–60 minutes for steaks.
Sear in a very hot, oiled pan for about a minute a side, edges included. No long rest needed: it was resting in the gentle oven.
